summary.text: Simcha Eichenstein is the Democratic and Conservative Party incumbent running unopposed for re-election in Assembly District 48, which includes Borough Park.
A former aide to New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli and to Mayor Bill de Blasio, he has held the seat since 2019, succeeding longtime Assemblyman Dov Hikind.
Ballotpedia lists his committees as Cities, Governmental Employees, Housing, Insurance, Real Property Taxation, and Social Services.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Eichenstein is a graduate of New York's yeshiva system and a lifelong resident of Borough Park.
Before elected office, he worked as political affairs director at a public relations firm, as a special assistant in the New York State legislature, and as a member of Brooklyn's Community Board 12.
He served for four years as a senior aide to State Comptroller Thomas P. DiNapoli, working on intergovernmental affairs and relations with community and non-profit organizations.

He then worked on Mayor Bill de Blasio's legislative affairs team in Albany and on the mayor's senior intergovernmental staff at City Hall, with a portfolio that included the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, the Department for the Aging, the Department of Homeless Services and NYC Health + Hospitals.

Eichenstein was elected on November 6, 2018, to represent the 48th Assembly District, which his official biography says includes Borough Park, Kensington and Midwood; the biography states he was the first Chassidic Jewish individual elected to the state legislature.
He assumed office on January 1, 2019, succeeding Dov Hikind.
He was appointed Assistant Majority Whip of the Assembly on the first day of the 2023 legislative session.

His official biography lists legislation he sponsored and passed, including exempting Summer Youth Employment Program earnings when calculating household income for public assistance eligibility, requiring state correctional facilities to offer kosher and halal options in commissaries and vending machines, and exempting first responders from monetary penalties for violations committed while responding to medical emergencies.

Throughout his tenure Eichenstein has served on the Housing, Cities, Governmental Employees, Real Property Taxation and Social Services committees, adding the Insurance Committee in the 2025-2026 session.
His official biography states that he and his wife, Pearl, have four children.
